clock_quality.rule: Rows without a transport key (2026-06-22..2026-07-14 polling era) have ts stamped by the feed at the poll: exact, available_utc = fetched_utc. Rows with transport angel_ws/angel_rest have ts = the exchange timestamp (Reading.ts), not a capture clock: published, available_utc = max(ts, exchFeedTime, exchTradeTime). Capture followed within the collector's freshness window for live rows (WS delivery; REST fetch - exchFeedTime <= 60 s) and with unbounded lag for delayed rows.

name: mcx_quotes
notes: Native unit: INR per exchange unit; gold 10 g, silver 1 kg, copper 1 kg, crude 1 bbl.

dated_contract rows come from the reading's dated-contract block (from 2026-09-07): the 2nd and 3rd dated contracts polled by REST in the same cycle; deduplicated on (ts, entry hash) separately from reading rows.
Empty depth levels (price 0, quantity 0, orders 0) are stored as null.

A websocket reading whose raw ts is its own last_traded_timestamp_ms read as milliseconds (1970-01-21; the feed stamped readings so on 2026-09-28 from 03:30 to 04:57 UTC, while Angel sends that field in seconds) is stamped with the instant the field states: fetched_utc, session_date and exch_trade_time_utc follow it, and available_utc stays the latest of the row's stamps, which is the exchange feed time.

Dropped raw keys with constant or duplicate content: contractEvidence.authenticatedSearchRow (= symbol/token), scripMasterRow.exch_seg/instrumenttype/strike/is_cas_enabled/name, resolved.* (= symbol/token/expiry), fullQuote.exchange/tradingSymbol/symbolToken, marginEvidence.source/currency/requestQuantity/nativeInstrument.
The broker account object of the raw rows is removed by the reader before typing; it never reaches a frame.
